title.narrative: Strengthening Conservation of Primary Forests through Partnership Enhancement and Coordination of Support

description.narrative: Knowledge management and learning planThe knowledge Management and learning (KM&L) plan intends to be a guidance document for stakeholders and project partners for use as an aid for effective knowledge use, dissemination, and action, not only limited to the archiving of knowledge generated by the project.The KM&L plan has the following main goals –1. To create awareness regarding the need for primary forest conservation.2. To contribute to evidence-based policy, and to build a shared understanding for the need for improved policies and practices for primary forest conservation.3. To mobilise actions and resources from countries, donors, GEF agencies, NGOs, Indigenous Peoples & Local Communities, women, youth, and other relevant stakeholders for primary forest conservation.Overall KM&L will be coordinated by IUCN. The Programme Associate part of the project management team at IUCN will coordinate the knowledge management of this project together with the Global Programme Manager with the support of the Executing Agencies (EAs). IUCN will develop a knowledge repository via a dedicated project website & will continue to maintain it even after project completion as part of IUCN’s work on Primary Forests including Intact Forest Landscapes. All the reports, policy guidance documents and workshop outcomes will be housed under this website. IUCN and EAs will also use innovative methods such as story maps, information videos and blogs to communicate the issues surrounding primary forests and lessons learnt from this project. This coordination has been outlined as IUCN’s role under Component 2 and in the Terms of Reference of the Programme Associate. Each executing agency will also ensure proper communication and dissemination of knowledge generated by this project via their own dissemination channels. Furthermore, the Collaborative Partnership on Forests (CPF) will also be leveraged to support the knowledge management and learning plan, with selected deliverables shared and promoted within the CPF website and networks.A draft KML plan with key deliverables, budget and the responsible executing agency(ies) has been proposed below which will be further refined during the inception phase: Knowledge Management and Learning (KML) Plan deliverables and budgetActivitiesDeliverablesBudgetExecuting agencyTimelineOutcome 1: Profile of primary forests raised globally and financing for their conservation facilitated, promoted and stimulated.Activity 1.1.1: Prepare policy recommendations targeting key policy sessions and conventions. The objective of this project is to prevent the loss of tropical primary forests worldwide by strengthening their protection and conservation, which will in turn contribute to mitigating climate change, preventing biodiversity loss and land degradation, while improving the livelihoods of the communities that depend upon them.
Problem and issues to be addressed:
Primary forests play a critical role in carbon storage and sequestration, biodiversity conservation and other ecosystem services, as well as livelihoods support. Their conservation is fundamental for achieving multiple global goals, including the UNSPF Global Forest Goals and the objectives of the CBD, UNFCCC, UNCCD and several SDGs.
Currently, there is insufficient recognition and conservation of primary forests globally, especially tropical primary forests. The lack of understanding and integration of the values and benefits of primary forests in global policy agendas and forest financing strategies has led to their inadequate prioritization, contributing to ongoing deforestation and loss of these vital ecosystems. Lack of coordination and information-sharing mechanisms has further hindered donor engagement and resulted in a funding gap that hampers effective conservation efforts.
The objective of this project will be accomplished through knowledge packaging and dissemination and capacity development that will raise the visibility of tropical primary forests among stakeholders, policymakers, and the public, transforming how they are perceived and ensuring their inclusion in forest financing strategies, conservation initiatives, and the global policy agenda. The project will also facilitate and stimulate financing for tropical primary forest conservation by establishing robust donor-recipient dialogue and coordination mechanisms and providing information on financing opportunities. The project seeks to enhance the work of the GFFFN, supporting countries in developing forest finance strategies that prioritize intact tropical primary forests. This transformative approach will strengthen financing mechanisms, foster innovative approaches, and mobilize resources towards the conservation of tropical primary forests.
The project aligns with the Collaborative Partnership on Forests (CPF) in enhancing coordination on global forest issues among relevant international forest-related organizations.
